Find the parametric equations of the hyperbola shown above given that its asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}x.$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
x=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t,
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants.

The vertices of the hyperbola occur at $(0,\pm a).$ From the graph, we have that $(0,\sqrt{3})$ is a vertex of the hyperbola, so $a=\sqrt{3}.$

Recall also that the asymptotes of the hyperbola occur at $y=\pm \frac{a}{b}x.$ In our case, the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}x.
$$

Equating the coefficients of $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{a}{b} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{b} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ b & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the hyperbola are

$$
x=2\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$
